seed: Give a row a width too small for what is in it and the pieces just hang out over the edge, with nothing anywhere saying so. The walk stacks three equal pieces into a row, squeezes the row, and reads the one line the Layout section now prints: which edge they run past, and the two things that would fix it.

steps.note: Three equal pieces as one row, 10 apart, as wide as they add up to. A row that is the size of its contents can never run out of room, so the Layout section says NOTHING about overflowing.

THE TEST: the row is 200 wide and its pieces run out past the right edge. The Layout section now says so in one line, and names both fixes: wrap the row, or make it 320 wide, which is the width that actually holds all three.

steps.reads: The pieces run past the right edge. Wrap them onto more lines, or make it 320 wide.

steps.note: THE TEST: taking the fix it offered makes everything fit, and the line goes away the same moment. Nothing is left nagging about a row that is now fine.
THE TEST: the other fix it named works too. Typing the 320 it asked for holds all three pieces, and the line goes away.

THE TEST: it is not a row-and-width thing. A row given a height too short for its pieces says the bottom edge instead, and names the height that would hold them. Wrapping is not offered here, because wrapping a row inside a fixed height only sends the new lines out of the bottom.

steps.reads: The pieces run past the bottom edge. Make it 40 tall.

steps.note: THE TEST: past both edges is still ONE line, naming both edges and one size. Two lines saying the same thing twice would read as the section stammering.

steps.reads: The pieces run past the right and bottom edges. Make it 320 × 40.
